options.title: Its own browser or computer tools
options.detail: Whatever your agent already has where you use it.

options.title: browser-harness
options.summary: Your agent drives your real Chrome: clicking, typing, signed-in pages, pages that need JavaScript.
options.why: Some pages only open in a browser you are signed in to. With this, your agent can open them the way you would.

network: none for your local Chrome; a cloud browser is optional and needs its own sign-in
writes: screenshots and action traces, only if you turn recording on
needs.firstRun: Chrome needs one tick at chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging; macOS may ask for Accessibility.

terms.summary: Some sites, video sites among them, don't allow automated access, including from your own browser. Your agent, not Cicada, is doing it.
safeUses: pages and accounts you may read yourself

options.cicadaNote: Cicada only asks your agent to use it. It can't see or limit what your agent does in your browser.
options.reach: Uses your own Chrome, including sites where you're signed in.

options.title: macos-harness
options.summary: Your agent controls apps on your Mac with screenshots, keyboard and mouse, not only the browser.
options.why: Some things only happen in a desktop app. With this, your agent can work in one the way you would.

network: none, unless your agent uses it with a website
writes: screenshots of your screen while it works
needs.firstRun: It checks its permissions with `macos-harness doctor` and asks before requesting any.
limits: Sends anonymous usage counts unless you run `macos-harness telemetry disable`.

terms.summary: Some sites, video sites among them, don't allow automated access, including from your own browser. Your agent, not Cicada, is doing it.
safeUses: pages and accounts you may read yourself

options.cicadaNote: Cicada only asks your agent to use it. It can't see or limit what your agent does on your Mac.
options.reach: Can control any app on your Mac. Needs Accessibility, Screen Recording and Automation access.

claude-code.prompt: Set up the macos-harness skill for me, then stop. Follow the install steps in install.md of https://github.com/browser-use/macos-harness at tag v0.1.2, but install the reviewed version: `uv tool install --python 3.12 macos-harness==0.1.2`. Register the skill that `macos-harness skill` prints under the name macos-harness, with no trigger sentence: do not make it your default for other tasks, I will ask for it when I want it. It can control apps on this Mac: ask me before you request any macOS permission, and ask whether to run `macos-harness telemetry disable` (it sends anonymous usage counts otherwise). options.title: Its own tools for watching
options.detail: Whatever your agent already has where you use it.

options.title: claude-video
options.summary: Your agent watches a video you point it at and tells you what's in it.
options.why: A saved video in Cicada is only a title. With this, your agent can look at the frames and captions when you ask, so you can talk about what a video actually says.

network: api.groq.com, only when a video has no captions
api.openai.com, only when a video has no captions
writes: a temporary folder holding the video while it works
hooks: In Claude Code, a short setup check each time a session starts
needs.firstRun: On a Mac it installs ffmpeg and yt-dlp with Homebrew the first time it runs.
limits: Reads English captions; other languages need one of the transcription keys.

terms.summary: It downloads videos with yt-dlp. YouTube's terms don't allow downloading or automated access without YouTube's permission.
safeUses: videos you made, like your own Looms

options.cicadaNote: Cicada itself never downloads video. It only keeps what your agent tells it afterwards.
options.reach: Downloads the video to a temporary folder on your Mac while it works.
options.detail: Your agent watches a video you point it at and tells you what's in it.
